texts.facts: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (Pfa Act), wherein it is alleged that the accused persons had sold /distributed / manufactured mis branded food in violation of Section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act read with Rule 37A(2) of PFA Rules, as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. In Re vs A-1) Sh. Hitesh Khatuja on 15 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144812211/ 2 2. As per the complaint, on 23.11.2007, the food officials including Food Inspector (FI) Sanjeev Kumar Gupta and Field Assistant (FA) Brahmanand under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. Ranjeet Singh reached at the premises of accused no. 5 M/s. K.M. Enterprises (partnership firm) at D-3, Progressive Chamber, D- Block, Central Market, Prashant Vihar, Delhi-110085, where the accused no. 1 in the capacity of its vendor-cum-partner was found conducting the business of various food articles, including 'Kitchen King', which was found stored for sale for human consumption, lying in sealed packets of 100 gm each bearing identical label declaration. The food officials lifted the sample the said food article consisting of 9 such sealed packets of Kitchen King ready for sale. It was divided into three parts as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules and separately packed and sealed. Necessary documents were prepared at the spot including the vendor's receipt and panchanama. Price of the sample was paid to the vendor. One counterpart of the sample was deposited with the Public Analyst (PA) and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 27.12.2007, the PA reported that the article was conforming to the standards, yet the sample was found misbranded being in violation of Rule 37A(2) of PFA Rules, because it was without declaration of name of food or category under which it fell. Based on the report of PA, investigation was carried out by the Food Inspector as per the instructions of the SDM/LHA. At the time of sampling, the accused no. 1 vendor had disclosed that the commodity had been supplied to him by M/s. Dalmia INC alias Manglam Traders (Proprietorship concern of accused no. 6), which had intern purchased it from M/s R.R. Enterprises (proprietorship concern of accused no.7). Investigation revealed that accused no. 5 firm had four partners (accused no. 1 to 4 herein), all of whom were implicated in the matter. Further, the food article had been supplied to the distributor accused no. 7 by accused no. 10 partnership firm, of which accused no. 8 and 9 were the partners. The food article had been manufactured by accused no. 12 company, of which accused no. 11 had been appointed as nominee under Section 17 of PFA Act. Hence, after obtaining due sanction of the Director, PFA, the present complaint came to be filed against all the accused persons for violation of the section 2(ix)(k) read with Rule 37A(2) of PFA Rules, as punishable under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act for selling /distributing / manufacturing misbranded food. 3. Since the complaint was filed by a public servant in writing, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned vide order dated 02.07.2008. Based on the report of PA, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed vide order dated 17.03.2010 against all the accused persons for commission of offence under Section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 4. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 Sh. Ranjeet Singh, PW-2 FI Sanjeev Kumar Gupta and PW-3 FI Raj Pal Singh were examined. PW-1 and PW-2 were a part of the team that had visited the premises of accused no. 5 (where accused no. 1 was the vendor) and lifted the sample of Kitchen King lying in sealed packets of 100 gm each. These witnesses deposed about the sample proceedings conducted by them on 23.11.2007 and narrated the steps undertaken by them, including disclosing their identity, lifting of 9 sealed packets of 100 gm each, dividing the same in three counterparts by putting 3 sealed packets as one counterpart and separately packing them. A sum of Rs.270/- was offered to the vendor as price of the sample vide vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A but the same was refused on the ground that the food article was not In Re vs A-1) Sh. Hitesh Khatuja on 15 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144812211/ 3 for sale and was used only for preparation of other food articles. Notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C were prepared at the spot. Based on the information given by the accused no. 1, notice under section 14A of PFA Act, Ex. PW-1/D was prepared addressed to accused no. 6. One counterpart was deposited with the PA vide receipt Ex. PW-1/F and remaining two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA vide receipt Ex. PW-1 / E. PA report Ex. PW-1/G was received opining the sample to be misbranded. Further investigation was carried out during which letters were written to the vendor, distributor, supplier, manufacturer and Government departments so as to ascertain their roles and involvement and their replies received. The said communications are Ex. PW-2/A to Ex. PW-2/H. Further investigation was carried out by PW-3 who also wrote letter Ex. PW-3/A to the STO and received reply Ex. PW-3/B. After completion of investigation, consent for prosecution Ex. PW-3/C was taken from the Director, PFA, after which the complaint Ex. PW-3/D was filed and intimation letter Ex. PW- 3/E was sent to the accused persons vide postal receipt Ex. PW-3/F. Vide order dated 14.09.2011, Ld. Defence Counsel admitted the role of FA upon which he was discharged unexamined and PE was closed. 5. PW-1 during cross-examination accepted that the samples were sealed and that the list of ingredients was also mentioned on the product. He went on to accept that Kitchen King was a popular name for Masala. PW-2 during cross-examination affirmed this fact, though he could not say if Kitchen King was popular name of Masala. PW-3 was not cross examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. Subsequently, several applications were moved under Section 294 CrPC which were disposed of vide order dated 11.09.2013 and the accused no. 1 to 6 were discharged. Record shows that similar applications were moved by accused no. 7 and 8 and the matter was listed for arguments on the applications. Order dated 18.11.2014 shows no objection of Ld. Counsel for accused no. 12, 10 and 8 if benefit of warranty was granted to the said applicants. However, no further orders were passed on the applications. 7. Statements of the accused no.7,8 (also representing accused no. 10) and 11 (also representing accused no.12) were recorded under section 313 CrPC on 04.04.2015 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. They expressed ignorance of sample proceedings on the ground that they were not present at that time. Accused no . 7 claimed that he had purchased the food article from accused no. 8 and had sold it in the same condition as purchased. Accused no. 8 and 10 also maintained that the food article had been procured from accused no. 12 and had supplied it in the same condition. Accused no. 12 and its nominee accused no. 11 disputed the PA report on the ground that there was nothing to mislead any customer and that there was no violation of any rule. No defence evidence was however led by them despite opportunity.
texts.arguments: 8. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to prove its case against all the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt, as all the witnesses have supported its case and there is no condition in their testimony. It is submitted that the accused persons have failed to rebut the findings as given by the PA. In Re vs A-1) Sh. Hitesh Khatuja on 15 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144812211/ 4 9. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused persons has submitted that the prosecution case fails on technical grounds. Ld. Counsel submits that there is no violation of any rule including Rule 37A(2) of PFA Rules as the name "Kitchen King" is a trade name of masala which is recognized by this name only. It is submitted that the food article was a proprietary food and all its ingredients had been mentioned on the label and therefore, no customer was misled in any manner.
